cards.text: Isaiah the prophet brings a new message from the LORD of Hosts. No small talk. No warm-up. It opens with an OATH: the LORD of Hosts has sworn.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts swears an oath about His plan. True or false: He says His plan might still change.

cards.text: He says, "Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand." Me? I've been "planning" to clean my oven so long the crumbs in there started paying RENT.
Then the LORD names who this plan is about: Assyria. Friend, when your name comes up right after the word "sworn," I don't think you're getting a cookie box.

cards.question: The LORD has sworn His plan will stand. What does He say He will do to Assyria in His land?
The LORD says He will trample Assyria on His ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about a yoke and a burden. Assyria has put them on somebody's shoulders.

cards.question: Whose shoulders does the LORD say Assyria's yoke and burden will be taken off?

cards.text: "His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders." You ever haul EVERY bag in from the car in one trip, arms shaking, till somebody finally lifts them off you? THAT. But for a whole people.
Then the message zooms way, WAY out.

cards.question: The message zooms out: this is the plan devised for the whole ___.
True or false: the message pictures the LORD's hand stretched out over all the nations.

cards.text: Then it ends with two questions, and they just hang there: "The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?"

cards.question: The message asks who can thwart the LORD of Hosts and who can turn His hand back. What answer do those questions expect?

answers.text: Only all the nations together can

cards.question: True or false: the message says a big enough army could turn back the LORD's outstretched hand.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Isaiah the prophet brings a new message from the LORD of Hosts." / "No small talk." / "No warm-up." / "It opens with an OATH..." The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Assyria appears here for the first time, but the card never says who Assyria is, such as the empire pressing on God's people, with its reference.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke says Assyria's name comes up "right after the word 'sworn.'" That isn't true of the text: the whole first half of the oath in 14:24 comes between "sworn" and "Assyria" in 14:25.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Card 4's setup joke ("I don't think you're getting a cookie box") signals bad news for Assyria. That rules out both wrong answers, which are favorable to Assyria ("Make a treaty with Assyria" and "Give Assyria more land"), so "Break Assyria" is the only answer left and stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word "mountain" from "I will trample him on My mountain" (14:25). No card has set it up, so the blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen rather than meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This card repeats 14:25 (the yoke and burden taken off God's people) right after cards 7 and 8 already covered it. It recaps instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
